title: Mathlib Imports for Asymptotic Analysis
content: Imports prime number basics, filter/limit machinery for $\limsup$/$\liminf$ (needed for asymptotic $o(1)$ statements), real number arithmetic, and general Lean tactics. The filter imports support the $\varepsilon$-$N$ formulation of the conjecture.
mathContext: The asymptotic statement $q(n,k) < (1+o(1))\log n$ is formalized using $\forall \varepsilon > 0,\, \exists N_0,\, \forall n \geq N_0$ rather than $\limsup$ directly, but the filter imports support potential future generalizations.

title: Consecutive Product Definition
content: Defines the product of $k$ consecutive integers starting from $n+1$ as a Finset product: $\mathrm{consecutiveProduct}(n,k) = \prod_{i=0}^{k-1}(n+i+1) = (n+1)(n+2)\cdots(n+k)$. This is the central arithmetic object whose prime divisors determine $q(n,k)$.

title: Axiomatized $q(n,k)$ Function
content: Declares $q(n,k)$ (smallestMissingPrime) as an axiom — a function $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ whose properties are specified separately. This axiomatization avoids the complexity of constructing the least prime not dividing a given number, which would require decidability of primality and divisibility search.

title: Three Axioms Characterizing $q(n,k)$
content: The function $q(n,k)$ is fully characterized by three axioms: (1) $q(n,k)$ is prime, (2) $q(n,k) \nmid (n+1)\cdots(n+k)$, and (3) every prime $p < q(n,k)$ divides the product. Together these uniquely determine $q(n,k)$ as the least prime not dividing the consecutive product.

title: Erdős Problem 663 — Main Conjecture
content: The central conjecture: for each fixed $k \geq 1$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$, the bound $q(n,k) < (1+\varepsilon)\log n$ holds for all sufficiently large $n$. This is a precise formalization of $q(n,k) < (1+o(1))\log n$, converting the asymptotic notation into a quantified statement.
mathContext: $\forall k \geq 1,\, \forall \varepsilon > 0,\, \exists N_0,\, \forall n \geq N_0: q(n,k) < (1+\varepsilon)\log n$

title: Weak Bound from Prime Number Theorem
content: The known weaker bound $q(n,k) < (1+o(1))\,k\log n$, which follows from the prime number theorem. By PNT, the number of primes up to $x$ is approximately $x/\log x$, so primes up to $k\log n$ number about $k\log n / \log(k\log n)$, and $k$ consecutive integers provide enough residue classes to cover all such primes.
mathContext: $\forall k \geq 1,\, \forall \varepsilon > 0,\, \exists N_0,\, \forall n \geq N_0: q(n,k) < (1+\varepsilon)\,k\log n$

title: Weak Bound Implies Conjecture for $k=1$
content: When $k=1$, the weak bound $(1+\varepsilon) \cdot 1 \cdot \log n = (1+\varepsilon)\log n$ coincides with the conjectured bound. The proof is a simple rewrite using `mul_one`. This shows the conjecture is trivially true for $k=1$ given the weak bound, and the real content lies in $k \geq 2$.
mathContext: $(1+\varepsilon) \cdot 1 \cdot \log n = (1+\varepsilon)\log n$, so the weak bound for $k=1$ is exactly the main conjecture for $k=1$.

title: Consecutive Product for $k=1$
content: For $k=1$, the consecutive product reduces to a single term: $(n+1)$. Proved by `simp` on the Finset.range definition. This grounds the abstract product definition in the simplest case.

title: Positivity of Consecutive Product
content: The consecutive product is always positive for $k > 0$, since each factor $n+i+1 \geq 1$. Proved using `Finset.prod_pos` with `omega` closing each positivity goal. This ensures the product is a valid nonzero natural number for divisibility arguments.

title: Connection to Erdős Problem #457
content: States the connection to Erdős Problem #457: among $k$ consecutive integers starting from $n+1$, there is always a prime $p \leq k+1$ dividing the product. This is a weaker but related structural property about small prime divisors of consecutive products, providing a floor for the prime coverage.
mathContext: $\forall k \geq 1,\, \forall n,\, \exists p \in \mathbb{P},\, p \leq k+1 \text{ and } p \mid (n+1)\cdots(n+k)$

title: Small Primes Divide Consecutive Products
content: Axiomatizes the pigeonhole principle for primes: if $p \leq k$, then $p$ divides $(n+1)(n+2)\cdots(n+k)$ because among any $k$ consecutive integers, at least one must be divisible by $p$ (since the residues $\bmod p$ cycle with period $p \leq k$).
mathContext: $\forall p \in \mathbb{P},\, p \leq k \Rightarrow p \mid \prod_{i=1}^{k}(n+i)$, since $\{n+1,\ldots,n+k\}$ contains a complete residue system $\bmod p$.

title: Lower Bound $q(n,k) > k$
content: For $k > 1$, the smallest missing prime exceeds $k$. This is an immediate consequence of small_prime_divides_product: every prime $p \leq k$ divides the product, so the least non-dividing prime must be strictly greater than $k$. This establishes a non-trivial lower bound on $q(n,k)$.
mathContext: $k > 1 \Rightarrow q(n,k) > k$, since all primes $p \leq k$ satisfy $p \mid (n+1)\cdots(n+k)$.

title: Monotonicity of $q$ in $k$
content: Axiomatizes that $q(n,k)$ is non-increasing in $k$: if $k_1 \leq k_2$, then $q(n,k_2) \leq q(n,k_1)$. Adding more consecutive terms can only introduce new prime factors, never remove them, so the smallest missing prime can only decrease (or stay the same).

title: Main Conjecture Implies Weak Bound
content: Proves that the main conjecture (without $k$ factor) implies the weak bound (with $k$ factor). The proof extracts the $N_0$ from the main conjecture and uses the chain of inequalities $(1+\varepsilon)\log n \leq (1+\varepsilon)\,k\log n$ since $k \geq 1$. Uses `mul_assoc`, `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left`, and `nlinarith` with the cast `Nat.cast_pos.mpr hk`.
